data.narrative:
GrayMatter Robotics is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $70M+ to date. The valuation analysis relies on a comparison universe of four same-sector and same/adjacent-stage private peers (Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Hadrian, and Nimble Robotics), supplemented by a broader comp set of eight private companies and one public comparable.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, anchored to the company's last known post-money valuation of $300M, applies a 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier, implying $570M. Peer-median analysis across the four core comparables yields $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $1.8B. The peer set reflects current market valuations for robotics companies at Series B and Series C stages.

The triangulated analysis produces a valuation range of $484M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $1.1B. The wide range reflects methodological divergence: stage-progression implies a more conservative midpoint aligned with typical step-up mechanics, while peer multiples suggest the market has valued comparable-stage robotics companies substantially higher. Key uncertainties include the recency and specificity of peer valuations relative to current market conditions, and whether GrayMatter's operational metrics and market position warrant positioning toward the upper or lower end of the peer distribution.
